facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin
A 42-year-old Taiwanese woman
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, or anorexia
medical history was negative for liver disease
smoked 2–5 cigarettes daily for ten years
afebrile, with no jaundice or lymphadenopathy
WBC 9950/µL
AST 37 U/L, ALT 82 U/L
HBsAg and anti-HCV were negative
multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver
epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments
diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E
negativity for cytokeratin

concepts.why: The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver, epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia, and diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E support this diagnosis.

The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver, epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia, and diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E support this diagnosis, although it is less common than metastasis.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver and elevated liver enzymes support this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for HCC.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver and elevated liver enzymes support this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for ICC.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver supports this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for common metastatic tumors.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver could support this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for hemangioma.
The presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver could support this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemical staining results are not typical for FNH.
The presence of fever and elevated white blood cell count could support this diagnosis, although the imaging results are not typical for liver abscess.
The presence of elevated liver enzymes could support this diagnosis, although the imaging results are not typical for cirrhosis.
The presence of elevated liver enzymes could support this diagnosis, although the imaging results are not typical for liver fibrosis.

rationales.F09: Multiple heterogeneous masses in the liver suggest a malignant process.
rationales.F10: Epithelioid tumor cells with melanin pigments are characteristic of melanoma.
rationales.F11: Immunohistochemical staining positive for melanoma markers confirms the diagnosis.
rationales.F12: Negativity for cytokeratin rules out carcinomas.

frontier_selector.rationale: diffuse positivity for HMB45, Melan-A, SOX10, and BRAF V600E, and epithelioid tumor cells with moderate nuclear atypia and focal intracytoplasmic melanin pigments, are highly specific for melanoma, and the presence of multiple heterogeneous masses in both lobes of the liver suggests metastasis rather than a primary hepatic tumor
